title: Canonical base-change stalks and restriction maps
statement: For p:X→S, g:T→S, a commutative coefficient ring Λ, q∈ℤ, F a sheaf of Λ-modules on T_et, and x∈X, define A(U) and B(U), for U→T, as the source and target geometric stalks of the canonical Cartesian square X×_S U. Let b_U:A(U)→B(U) be its base-change map. For a morphism φ:U→V over T, define r_φ:B(V)→B(U) by the target transition through the canonical pullback lift followed by the inverse-image composition isomorphism. For any original Cartesian square sq with base g define t_U from its target stalk to B(U) by the canonical pullback lift. These are wrappers for the existing transition maps and geometric stalk functor, with no new choices.

source.place: Tags 0F07 (restriction square and limit condition) and 09Z1 (higher direct image continuity)

Existing higherDirectImage_limit supplies stalk continuity for higher images, but not source inverse-image/homology identification or target pullback/coefficient identification. Existing target composition and base-change naturality supply the two proved compatibility lemmas. No canonical stalk wrappers or source-image descent/target-zero detection declarations found.
